hints: Focus on what oxidation means for an aldehyde, gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen to form a carboxylic acid.
Notice that reaction 1 adds HCN across the C=O bond to make a cyanohydrin, so the oxidation state of carbon does not increase.
Recall what Tollens and Fehling test for, and check which two reactions convert an aldehyde to a carboxylate with reduction of silver or copper.
walkthrough:
**Check reaction 1 for oxidation**

Think of oxidation as an increase in oxidation number. In addition of HCN to ethanal, no oxygen is gained and no hydrogen is lost overall.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$$
This is nucleophilic addition to form a cyanohydrin, not oxidation.

**Check reaction 2 with Tollens reagent**

Tollens reagent contains $\text{Ag}^+$ in ammonia. Aldehydes reduce it to silver metal while they are oxidised to carboxylate ions.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + 2\text{Ag}^+ + 3\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^- + 2\text{Ag} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So the aldehyde is oxidised, silver mirror forms.

**Check reaction 3 with Fehling reagent**

Fehling reagent contains blue $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ complex. Aldehydes reduce it to brick-red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ while they are oxidised to carboxylate.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + 2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So the aldehyde is oxidised here too.

**Combine the conclusions**

Only 2 and 3 involve oxidation. Reaction 1 is addition. That matches the combination of 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This says 1, 2 and 3 are all oxidations. Reactions 2 and 3 are correct, but 1 with HCN is nucleophilic addition to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$, not oxidation.
options.B: Incorrect. This says 1 and 2 only. Reaction 2 is oxidation, but reaction 1 is not oxidation, and it wrongly leaves out reaction 3 which is a classic aldehyde oxidation.
options.C: Correct. Both Tollens reagent oxidises $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ to a carboxylate with Ag mirror, and Fehling reagent oxidises $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ to a carboxylate with red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$. Reaction 1 is only addition.
options.D: Incorrect. This says 1 only. Reaction 1 with HCN shows no change in oxidation level, it is addition across C=O. The true oxidations are 2 and 3.
